Gurukulam Reviving Ancient Wisdom

Home Programs Books Campus Gallery Keyboard
About
About Us Our Mission Our Team
Contact
Our Sacred Learning Space Experience the tranquility of our traditional Gurukul campus nestled in the foothills of the Himalayas.
Campus Overview A harmonious blend of traditional architecture and natural surroundings
Our Gurukulam campus is designed following ancient Vastu principles, creating an environment conducive to learning and spiritual growth. Spread across 10 acres of lush greenery, the campus offers a serene atmosphere where students can immerse themselves in Vedic studies away from the distractions of modern life. The campus architecture reflects traditional Indian design elements, with spacious courtyards, meditation halls, and learning spaces that blend harmoniously with nature. Every aspect of the campus is thoughtfully designed to support the holistic development of our students.
Our Facilities Modern amenities within a traditional learning environment
Residential Quarters Simple, comfortable living spaces designed for focus and reflection. Each residence houses 4-6 students with shared amenities and study areas.
Learning Halls Traditional open halls (Shalas) where students gather to learn from teachers, with natural lighting and ventilation creating an ideal learning atmosphere.
Meditation Spaces Dedicated areas for meditation and spiritual practices, including a central temple and various smaller shrines throughout the campus.
Organic Gardens Extensive herb and vegetable gardens where students learn sustainable farming practices while growing food for the campus kitchen.
Sattvic Kitchen Our kitchen serves pure vegetarian, sattvic meals prepared with ingredients from our organic gardens, following traditional Ayurvedic principles.
Ancient Library A collection of rare manuscripts, Vedic texts, and contemporary resources on Sanskrit, philosophy, and ancient wisdom traditions.
Life at Gurukulam Experience the rhythmic flow of traditional gurukul living
4:30 AM
Brahma Muhurta The day begins early with the auspicious morning hour dedicated to meditation and self-study.
6:00 AM
Yoga Practice Morning yoga session to energize the body and prepare the mind for learning.
7:30 AM
Morning Prayers & Breakfast Community prayers followed by a nutritious sattvic breakfast.
9:00 AM - 12:30 PM
Morning Classes Intensive learning sessions in Sanskrit, Vedic texts, and philosophy.
1:00 PM
Midday Meal & Rest The main meal of the day followed by a short rest period.
3:00 PM - 5:30 PM
Afternoon Sessions Practical application of morning lessons, discussions, and specialized workshops.
6:00 PM
Evening Prayers Gathering for traditional fire ceremony (Agnihotra) and chanting.
7:00 PM
Light Dinner A simple evening meal followed by community activities or self-study.
9:30 PM
Rest Early retirement to prepare for the next day's early start.

Student Residences

Community Dining Hall
Experience Our Campus in Person Visit us for a guided tour and experience the transformative environment of our Gurukulam Book a Visit
Finding Us Our campus is located in the serene foothills of Rishikesh
Address Gurukulam Campus, Near Laxman Jhula,Rishikesh, Uttarakhand 249302, India Getting Here
By Air: The nearest airport is Jolly Grant Airport (Dehradun), approximately 35 km from our campus. By Train: Rishikesh Railway Station is 12 km from our campus. We can arrange pickup on request. By Road: Regular buses connect Rishikesh to major cities like Delhi (240 km) and Haridwar (25 km).
Shuttle Service We provide a free shuttle service from Rishikesh town to our campus at scheduled times. Please contact us in advance to arrange pickup. Contact for Directions

page.title: Sanatan Dharma Research Platform
page.raw_content:
Empowering Research and Knowledge Sharing in Sanatan Dharma A platform dedicated to exploring, preserving, and sharing the timeless wisdom of Sanatan Dharma through rigorous research and community collaboration.
Introduction Why It Matters Vision & Mission Features Join Us
Introduction Sanatan Dharma (often referred to as Hinduism) is one of the world's oldest living traditions, with a vast repository of scriptures, philosophies, and practices. Yet, in the modern age, much of its profound wisdom remains scattered, misinterpreted, or inaccessible to sincere seekers. This platform is dedicated to bridging that gap—by fostering a community of educated individuals, scholars, and practitioners who are passionate about exploring, preserving, and sharing the timeless knowledge of Sanatan Dharma.
Why This Initiative Matters Many ancient texts and teachings are either locked in Sanskrit or diluted by misinterpretations. Modern academia often lacks traditional insights, while traditional circles sometimes resist critical inquiry. A unified, research-driven platform can help:
Preserve authentic knowledge. Encourage intellectual and spiritual growth. Counter misinformation with well-researched content.
Our Vision & Mission Vision To create the world's most authentic, accessible, and intellectually rigorous platform for Sanatan Dharma—where tradition meets critical scholarship. Mission
Promote evidence-based research on scriptures, history, and philosophy. Facilitate respectful dialogue between scholars, practitioners, and seekers. Build a digital library of trusted translations, commentaries, and resources.
Key Features of the Platform
📚 In-Depth Research & Scholarship
Peer-reviewed articles on Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Darshanas (philosophical systems), and more. Comparative studies between Sanatan Dharma and other world traditions. Historical & archaeological research on Hindu civilization, temple architecture, and lost sciences.
🖥️ Knowledge Repository (Free & Open Access)
Digital library of scriptures (with multiple translations and commentaries). Video lectures by traditional scholars and academic experts. Podcasts & interviews on Yoga, Ayurveda, Vedanta, Tantra, and Jyotisha.
💬 Interactive Learning & Community
Discussion forums for debates on Dharma, ethics, and modern applications. Q&A sessions with scholars and gurus. Study groups (e.g., Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads, or Sanskrit learning circles).
🧘 Resources for Beginners & Seekers
Simplified guides on core concepts (Karma, Dharma, Moksha, Bhakti). Paths of Yoga (Bhakti, Jnana, Karma, Raja) explained in practical terms. Temple traditions, rituals, and festivals decoded.
Ensuring Authenticity & Depth
Collaboration with traditional acharyas and academic researchers to avoid misinterpretations. Encouraging Sanskrit literacy for deeper engagement with original texts. Cross-referencing ancient commentaries (Bhashyas) to maintain accuracy.
Modern Relevance & Outreach
Addressing contemporary issues (e.g., Hinduism and science, environmental Dharma, combating Hinduphobia). Multilingual support (English, Hindi, Tamil, Sanskrit, etc.) for wider reach. Social media presence with digestible, shareable content.
Join the Movement This platform thrives on community participation. Whether you are:
• A scholar researching Hindu texts, • A practitioner seeking deeper understanding, • Or a curious seeker exploring Dharma for the first time—
Your voice matters.
📖 Contribute articles 🎤 Suggest topics 💬 Join discussions
Let's work together to preserve, explore, and share the eternal wisdom of Sanatan Dharma! Subscribe for updates & join our community today!
Empowering Research and Knowledge Sharing in Sanatan Dharma
📱 📘 🐦 📸
© 2025-28 All Rights Reserved

Peer-reviewed articles on Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Darshanas (philosophical systems), and more. Comparative studies between Sanatan Dharma and other world traditions. Historical & archaeological research on Hindu civilization, temple architecture, and lost sciences.
🖥️ Knowledge Repository (Free & Open Access)
Digital library of scriptures (with multiple translations and commentaries). Video lectures by traditional scholars and academic experts. Podcasts & interviews on Yoga, Ayurveda, Vedanta, Tantra, and Jyotisha.
💬 Interactive Learning & Community
Discussion forums for debates on Dharma, ethics, and modern applications. Q&A sessions with scholars and gurus. Study groups (e.g., Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads, or Sanskrit learning circles).
🧘 Resources for Beginners & Seekers
Simplified guides on core concepts (Karma, Dharma, Moksha, Bhakti). Paths of Yoga (Bhakti, Jnana, Karma, Raja) explained in practical terms. Temple traditions, rituals, and festivals decoded.

section.heading: Ensuring Authenticity & Depth
section.raw_text:
Ensuring Authenticity & Depth
Collaboration with traditional acharyas and academic researchers to avoid misinterpretations. Encouraging Sanskrit literacy for deeper engagement with original texts. Cross-referencing ancient commentaries (Bhashyas) to maintain accuracy.
Modern Relevance & Outreach
Addressing contemporary issues (e.g., Hinduism and science, environmental Dharma, combating Hinduphobia). Multilingual support (English, Hindi, Tamil, Sanskrit, etc.) for wider reach. Social media presence with digestible, shareable content.

page.title: Sanatan Dharma - Vision & Mission
page.raw_content:
Our Vision & Mission Building bridges between ancient wisdom and modern scholarship
🌿 Vision To establish the world's most authentic, accessible, and interdisciplinary platform for Sanatan Dharma—bridging ancient wisdom with modern scholarship to combat misinformation, preserve endangered knowledge, and foster global understanding.
Why This Matters:
Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2021) 67% of online content about Hinduism contains inaccuracies or oversimplifications.
UNESCO Report Less than 5% of Sanskrit manuscripts have been digitized or translated, risking permanent loss of texts.
Pew Research (2023) While 80% of Hindus value traditional knowledge, only 12% have access to scholarly resources beyond local temples.
🎯 Mission Our mission is structured around three pillars, backed by data-driven strategies:
1 Promote Evidence-Based Research Goals:
Peer-reviewed scholarship: Collaborate with institutions like BHU, IIT Kharagpur, and Harvard's Divinity School Scientific parallels in Vedic texts (e.g., NASA's acknowledgment of Surya Siddhanta's astronomical accuracy) Archaeological validation of Hindu civilizational sites (e.g., recent underwater discoveries of Dwarka) Fact-checking hub to counter misinformation
JAAR Study (2022) Interdisciplinary research on Dharma increases public engagement by 300% compared to theological studies alone.
2 Facilitate Respectful Dialogue Goals:
Global symposia with advocates, academics, and spiritual leaders Digital forums on contentious topics with moderated debates Youth outreach through Dharma campuses and student councils
MIT Media Lab (2023) Structured interfaith dialogues reduce prejudice by 42% among participants.
3 Build a Digital Library Goals:
Open-access repository of 10,000+ texts by 2030 Multimedia archives of endangered oral traditions AI-powered tools for Sanskrit text analysis
Internet Archive Data 400% surge in downloads of Indic texts since 2020, signaling massive unmet demand.
🌟 Strategic Impact By 2030, we aim to:
📜 Train 1,000+ scholars In manuscript preservation (partnering with National Mission for Manuscripts)
🌍 Reach 5 million seekers Annually via multilingual content (prioritizing Hindi, Tamil, Bengali)
🔍 Top Google result For "Sanatan Dharma research" (SEO-optimized with 10,000+ backlinks)
Join us in this knowledge revolution—where every scripture decoded and every myth dispelled strengthens Dharma for future generations. Become Part of Our Mission

page.title: Timeless Wisdom: Hindu Scriptures and Their Relevance Today
page.raw_content:
Timeless Wisdom Exploring Hindu Ancient Scriptures and Their Relevance Today
Introduction Hinduism, one of the world's oldest religions, boasts a rich collection of ancient scriptures that continue to inspire millions. These texts, written in Sanskrit and other ancient languages, encompass a wide range of philosophical, spiritual, and practical teachings. In this blog, we will explore some of the most significant Hindu scriptures and their relevance in the modern world.
1. The Vedas: The Foundation of Hindu Wisdom The Vedas are the oldest and most authoritative Hindu scriptures, composed between 1500 and 500 BCE. They consist of four main texts: the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda. These texts contain hymns, rituals, and philosophical insights that form the bedrock of Hindu thought. The Four Vedas Rigveda The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and consists of 1,028 hymns dedicated to various deities. It emphasizes the importance of cosmic order (Rta) and the interconnectedness of all life.
"Truth is one; the wise call it by many names." – Rigveda 1.164.46
Story: The story of the sage Dirghatamas in the Rigveda highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding the universe's mysteries. Yajurveda The Yajurveda contains ritualistic formulas and mantras used during sacrifices. It bridges the gap between the Rigveda's hymns and the practical application of rituals. Modern Application: The Yajurveda's emphasis on rituals can inspire structured living and mindfulness in daily routines. Samaveda The Samaveda is a collection of melodies and chants derived from the Rigveda. It highlights the importance of sound and music in spiritual practice. Modern Application: The use of music in meditation and therapy today reflects the Samaveda's teachings on the power of sound. Atharvaveda The Atharvaveda includes spells, charms, and practical guidance for daily life. It addresses topics like health, relationships, and prosperity. Story: The story of the sage Atharvan, who discovered fire, symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge and innovation. Relevance Today The Vedas emphasize the interconnectedness of all life, a concept that resonates with modern environmentalism. Mantras from the Vedas, such as the Gayatri Mantra, are still widely chanted for spiritual upliftment and mental peace. Modern Application: The Gayatri Mantra is used in meditation practices worldwide to promote focus and inner peace.
2. The Upanishads: The Essence of Philosophical Inquiry The Upanishads, often referred to as Vedanta, explore the nature of reality, the self (Atman), and the ultimate reality (Brahman). Key Upanishads include the Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, and Katha Upanishads. Key Teachings Atman and Brahman The Upanishads teach that the individual soul (Atman) is identical to the universal consciousness (Brahman). This non-dualistic philosophy is central to Advaita Vedanta.
"Tat Tvam Asi" (Thou art That) – Chandogya Upanishad
Story: The story of Nachiketa in the Katha Upanishad illustrates the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and the importance of perseverance. Paths to Liberation The Upanishads outline various paths to liberation (Moksha), including knowledge (Jnana), devotion (Bhakti), and action (Karma). Modern Application: The practice of mindfulness meditation draws heavily from the Upanishadic emphasis on self-awareness. Relevance Today The Upanishads promote self-inquiry and introspection, which are central to modern mindfulness and meditation practices. Their teachings on non-duality inspire a sense of unity and oneness, addressing modern issues of division and conflict. Modern Application: The concept of "oneness" is increasingly relevant in promoting global harmony and environmental sustainability.
3. The Bhagavad Gita: A Guide to Life and Duty Part of the epic Mahabharata, the Bhagavad Gita is a dialogue between Lord Krishna and the warrior Arjuna. It addresses duty (Dharma), righteousness, and the paths to spiritual realization. Key Teachings Karma Yoga Krishna advises Arjuna to perform his duty without attachment to results. This teaching is central to the concept of Karma Yoga.
"You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of work." – Bhagavad Gita 2.47
Story: Arjuna's dilemma on the battlefield symbolizes the internal conflicts we face in life, and Krishna's guidance offers a roadmap for ethical decision-making. Bhakti Yoga The Gita emphasizes devotion (Bhakti) as a path to spiritual realization. Krishna declares that those who surrender to Him with love and devotion attain liberation. Modern Application: The principles of Bhakti Yoga inspire acts of kindness, charity, and community service. Relevance Today The Gita's teachings on performing one's duty without attachment to results are highly applicable in modern professional and personal life. It provides guidance on managing stress, ethical dilemmas, and decision-making. Modern Application: Corporate leaders often turn to the Gita for insights on ethical leadership and decision-making.
4. The Ramayana: A Tale of Righteousness and Devotion Authored by Valmiki, the Ramayana narrates the life of Lord Rama, his exile, and his battle against the demon king Ravana. It is a story of righteousness, loyalty, and the triumph of good over evil. Key Teachings Dharma and Loyalty Rama's adherence to Dharma, even in the face of personal hardship, serves as a model for righteous living.
"Rama's life is a testament to the power of righteousness and devotion."
Story: The story of Rama's exile and Sita's abduction highlights the importance of integrity and resilience. Hanuman's Devotion Hanuman's unwavering devotion to Rama symbolizes the ideal of selfless service and loyalty. Modern Application: Hanuman's story inspires individuals to overcome challenges with courage and humility. Relevance Today The Ramayana serves as a moral guide, emphasizing virtues like integrity, loyalty, and respect for elders. It highlights the importance of balancing personal and societal responsibilities. Modern Application: The Ramayana is often referenced in discussions on leadership and ethical governance.
5. The Mahabharata: The Epic of Human Emotions The Mahabharata, attributed to Vyasa, is an epic that includes the Bhagavad Gita. It explores complex human emotions, relationships, and ethical dilemmas through the story of the Kurukshetra war. Key Teachings Moral Ambiguity The Mahabharata portrays the complexity of human nature, where characters often face morally ambiguous situations.
"The Mahabharata teaches us that life is a series of choices, each with its own consequences."
Story: The story of Karna, who faced discrimination despite his noble qualities, highlights the importance of empathy and justice. Draupadi's Resilience Draupadi's strength in the face of injustice serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up for one's rights. Modern Application: Draupadi's story is often cited in discussions on gender equality and women's empowerment. Relevance Today The Mahabharata's portrayal of moral ambiguity and ethical conflicts mirrors modern societal challenges. Characters like Draupadi and Karna offer lessons on resilience and dignity in adversity. Modern Application: The Mahabharata is often referenced in discussions on ethics and justice.
6. The Puranas: Stories of Gods and Goddesses The Puranas are a collection of stories and myths that explain Hindu cosmology, deities, and traditions. Major Puranas include the Vishnu Purana, Shiva Purana, and Devi Bhagavata Purana. Key Teachings Cosmology and Creation The Puranas describe the creation of the universe and the cycles of time.
"The Puranas bring the divine into the realm of the human, making spirituality accessible to all."
Story: The story of Durga's victory over Mahishasura symbolizes the triumph of good over evil and continues to inspire devotees during festivals like Navratri. Devotion and Festivals The Puranas emphasize the importance of devotion (Bhakti) and celebrate the divine through festivals and rituals. Modern Application: Festivals like Navratri and Diwali are rooted in Puranic stories and continue to be celebrated worldwide. Relevance Today The Puranas make complex philosophical concepts accessible through storytelling. They preserve cultural and religious traditions, fostering a sense of identity and continuity. Modern Application: The Puranas inspire art, literature, and cultural practices across the globe.
7. The Dharmashastras: Codes of Conduct These texts, such as the Manusmriti, provide guidelines on law, ethics, and social duties. While some aspects are controversial and outdated, they offer insights into ancient societal structures. Key Teachings Ethical Governance The Dharmashastras emphasize the importance of justice, fairness, and ethical governance.
"The ruler who governs with justice earns the love of his people."
Story: The story of King Harishchandra, who upheld truth and justice despite personal suffering, serves as a model for ethical leadership. Social Duties These texts outline the duties of individuals based on their stage of life (Ashrama) and social role (Varna). Modern Application: The emphasis on justice and fairness in these texts remains relevant in modern legal and ethical frameworks. Relevance Today The Dharmashastras highlight the importance of ethical governance and social responsibility. They encourage reflection on the evolution of societal norms and values. Modern Application: The Dharmashastras inspire discussions on social justice and ethical governance.
8. The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali: The Science of Yoga This text systematizes the practice of Yoga, outlining the eight limbs of Yoga (Ashtanga Yoga) as a path to self-realization. Key Teachings Ashtanga Yoga The eight limbs of Yoga include ethical principles (Yamas and Niyamas), physical postures (Asanas), breath control (Pranayama), and meditation (Dhyana).
"Yoga is the stilling of the fluctuations of the mind." – Yoga Sutras 1.2
Story: The story of Patanjali, who is said to have incarnated to teach Yoga, highlights the transformative power of this practice. Inner Peace The Yoga Sutras emphasize the importance of inner peace and self-realization. Modern Application: Yoga has become a global phenomenon, with millions practicing it for health and wellness. Relevance Today The Yoga Sutras offer a practical guide to mental and physical well-being. They provide tools for managing stress, cultivating mindfulness, and deepening self-awareness. Modern Application: Yoga is widely practiced for its physical, mental, and spiritual benefits.
Conclusion Hindu ancient scriptures offer timeless wisdom that continues to guide individuals in their spiritual, ethical, and personal journeys. By exploring these texts, we can gain insights into living a balanced, purposeful, and fulfilling life in the modern world.

section.heading: Introduction
section.raw_text: Introduction Hinduism, one of the world's oldest religions, boasts a rich collection of ancient scriptures that continue to inspire millions. These texts, written in Sanskrit and other ancient languages, encompass a wide range of philosophical, spiritual, and practical teachings. In this blog, we will explore some of the most significant Hindu scriptures and their relevance in the modern world.
section.text: Introduction Hinduism, one of the world's oldest religions, boasts a rich collection of ancient scriptures that continue to inspire millions. These texts, written in Sanskrit and other ancient languages, encompass a wide range of philosophical, spiritual, and practical teachings. In this blog, we will explore some of the most significant Hindu scriptures and their relevance in the modern world.

section.heading: 1. The Vedas: The Foundation of Hindu Wisdom
section.raw_text:
1. The Vedas: The Foundation of Hindu Wisdom The Vedas are the oldest and most authoritative Hindu scriptures, composed between 1500 and 500 BCE. They consist of four main texts: the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda. These texts contain hymns, rituals, and philosophical insights that form the bedrock of Hindu thought. The Four Vedas Rigveda The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and consists of 1,028 hymns dedicated to various deities. It emphasizes the importance of cosmic order (Rta) and the interconnectedness of all life.
"Truth is one; the wise call it by many names." – Rigveda 1.164.46
Story: The story of the sage Dirghatamas in the Rigveda highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding the universe's mysteries. Yajurveda The Yajurveda contains ritualistic formulas and mantras used during sacrifices. It bridges the gap between the Rigveda's hymns and the practical application of rituals. Modern Application: The Yajurveda's emphasis on rituals can inspire structured living and mindfulness in daily routines. Samaveda The Samaveda is a collection of melodies and chants derived from the Rigveda. It highlights the importance of sound and music in spiritual practice. Modern Application: The use of music in meditation and therapy today reflects the Samaveda's teachings on the power of sound. Atharvaveda The Atharvaveda includes spells, charms, and practical guidance for daily life. It addresses topics like health, relationships, and prosperity. Story: The story of the sage Atharvan, who discovered fire, symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge and innovation. Relevance Today The Vedas emphasize the interconnectedness of all life, a concept that resonates with modern environmentalism. Mantras from the Vedas, such as the Gayatri Mantra, are still widely chanted for spiritual upliftment and mental peace. Modern Application: The Gayatri Mantra is used in meditation practices worldwide to promote focus and inner peace.

section.heading: 2. The Upanishads: The Essence of Philosophical Inquiry
section.raw_text:
2. The Upanishads: The Essence of Philosophical Inquiry The Upanishads, often referred to as Vedanta, explore the nature of reality, the self (Atman), and the ultimate reality (Brahman). Key Upanishads include the Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, and Katha Upanishads. Key Teachings Atman and Brahman The Upanishads teach that the individual soul (Atman) is identical to the universal consciousness (Brahman). This non-dualistic philosophy is central to Advaita Vedanta.
"Tat Tvam Asi" (Thou art That) – Chandogya Upanishad
Story: The story of Nachiketa in the Katha Upanishad illustrates the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and the importance of perseverance. Paths to Liberation The Upanishads outline various paths to liberation (Moksha), including knowledge (Jnana), devotion (Bhakti), and action (Karma). Modern Application: The practice of mindfulness meditation draws heavily from the Upanishadic emphasis on self-awareness. Relevance Today The Upanishads promote self-inquiry and introspection, which are central to modern mindfulness and meditation practices. Their teachings on non-duality inspire a sense of unity and oneness, addressing modern issues of division and conflict. Modern Application: The concept of "oneness" is increasingly relevant in promoting global harmony and environmental sustainability.

section.heading: 3. The Bhagavad Gita: A Guide to Life and Duty
section.raw_text:
3. The Bhagavad Gita: A Guide to Life and Duty Part of the epic Mahabharata, the Bhagavad Gita is a dialogue between Lord Krishna and the warrior Arjuna. It addresses duty (Dharma), righteousness, and the paths to spiritual realization. Key Teachings Karma Yoga Krishna advises Arjuna to perform his duty without attachment to results. This teaching is central to the concept of Karma Yoga.
"You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of work." – Bhagavad Gita 2.47
Story: Arjuna's dilemma on the battlefield symbolizes the internal conflicts we face in life, and Krishna's guidance offers a roadmap for ethical decision-making. Bhakti Yoga The Gita emphasizes devotion (Bhakti) as a path to spiritual realization. Krishna declares that those who surrender to Him with love and devotion attain liberation. Modern Application: The principles of Bhakti Yoga inspire acts of kindness, charity, and community service. Relevance Today The Gita's teachings on performing one's duty without attachment to results are highly applicable in modern professional and personal life. It provides guidance on managing stress, ethical dilemmas, and decision-making. Modern Application: Corporate leaders often turn to the Gita for insights on ethical leadership and decision-making.

section.heading: 4. The Ramayana: A Tale of Righteousness and Devotion
section.raw_text:
4. The Ramayana: A Tale of Righteousness and Devotion Authored by Valmiki, the Ramayana narrates the life of Lord Rama, his exile, and his battle against the demon king Ravana. It is a story of righteousness, loyalty, and the triumph of good over evil. Key Teachings Dharma and Loyalty Rama's adherence to Dharma, even in the face of personal hardship, serves as a model for righteous living.
"Rama's life is a testament to the power of righteousness and devotion."
Story: The story of Rama's exile and Sita's abduction highlights the importance of integrity and resilience. Hanuman's Devotion Hanuman's unwavering devotion to Rama symbolizes the ideal of selfless service and loyalty. Modern Application: Hanuman's story inspires individuals to overcome challenges with courage and humility. Relevance Today The Ramayana serves as a moral guide, emphasizing virtues like integrity, loyalty, and respect for elders. It highlights the importance of balancing personal and societal responsibilities. Modern Application: The Ramayana is often referenced in discussions on leadership and ethical governance.

section.heading: 5. The Mahabharata: The Epic of Human Emotions
section.raw_text:
5. The Mahabharata: The Epic of Human Emotions The Mahabharata, attributed to Vyasa, is an epic that includes the Bhagavad Gita. It explores complex human emotions, relationships, and ethical dilemmas through the story of the Kurukshetra war. Key Teachings Moral Ambiguity The Mahabharata portrays the complexity of human nature, where characters often face morally ambiguous situations.
"The Mahabharata teaches us that life is a series of choices, each with its own consequences."
Story: The story of Karna, who faced discrimination despite his noble qualities, highlights the importance of empathy and justice. Draupadi's Resilience Draupadi's strength in the face of injustice serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up for one's rights. Modern Application: Draupadi's story is often cited in discussions on gender equality and women's empowerment. Relevance Today The Mahabharata's portrayal of moral ambiguity and ethical conflicts mirrors modern societal challenges. Characters like Draupadi and Karna offer lessons on resilience and dignity in adversity. Modern Application: The Mahabharata is often referenced in discussions on ethics and justice.

section.heading: 6. The Puranas: Stories of Gods and Goddesses
section.raw_text:
6. The Puranas: Stories of Gods and Goddesses The Puranas are a collection of stories and myths that explain Hindu cosmology, deities, and traditions. Major Puranas include the Vishnu Purana, Shiva Purana, and Devi Bhagavata Purana. Key Teachings Cosmology and Creation The Puranas describe the creation of the universe and the cycles of time.
"The Puranas bring the divine into the realm of the human, making spirituality accessible to all."
Story: The story of Durga's victory over Mahishasura symbolizes the triumph of good over evil and continues to inspire devotees during festivals like Navratri. Devotion and Festivals The Puranas emphasize the importance of devotion (Bhakti) and celebrate the divine through festivals and rituals. Modern Application: Festivals like Navratri and Diwali are rooted in Puranic stories and continue to be celebrated worldwide. Relevance Today The Puranas make complex philosophical concepts accessible through storytelling. They preserve cultural and religious traditions, fostering a sense of identity and continuity. Modern Application: The Puranas inspire art, literature, and cultural practices across the globe.

section.heading: 7. The Dharmashastras: Codes of Conduct
section.raw_text:
7. The Dharmashastras: Codes of Conduct These texts, such as the Manusmriti, provide guidelines on law, ethics, and social duties. While some aspects are controversial and outdated, they offer insights into ancient societal structures. Key Teachings Ethical Governance The Dharmashastras emphasize the importance of justice, fairness, and ethical governance.
"The ruler who governs with justice earns the love of his people."
Story: The story of King Harishchandra, who upheld truth and justice despite personal suffering, serves as a model for ethical leadership. Social Duties These texts outline the duties of individuals based on their stage of life (Ashrama) and social role (Varna). Modern Application: The emphasis on justice and fairness in these texts remains relevant in modern legal and ethical frameworks. Relevance Today The Dharmashastras highlight the importance of ethical governance and social responsibility. They encourage reflection on the evolution of societal norms and values. Modern Application: The Dharmashastras inspire discussions on social justice and ethical governance.

mala.title: Shlok Mala 1
प्रथम श्लोक माला
mala.description: Selected Ramayana Shlokas with Audio Recitations by Dr. Ranganji (WEBOLIM)

shloka.raw_text: मानिषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौंचमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥ 1॥ हे निषाद! तूने काममोहित क्रौंच पक्षी के जोड़े में से एक को मारा है, इसलिए तुझे चिरस्थायी प्रतिष्ठा प्राप्त नहीं होगी। O Hunter, since you have killed one of this pair of Krauncha birds, overwhelmed by passion, you shall not attain lasting fame for endless years.

shloka.sanskrit: मानिषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौंचमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥ 1॥
shloka.hindi: हे निषाद! तूने काममोहित क्रौंच पक्षी के जोड़े में से एक को मारा है, इसलिए तुझे चिरस्थायी प्रतिष्ठा प्राप्त नहीं होगी।
shloka.english: O Hunter, since you have killed one of this pair of Krauncha birds, overwhelmed by passion, you shall not attain lasting fame for endless years.

shloka.raw_text: ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ । नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु पंचसु ॥ 2॥ तत्पश्चात् बारहवें महीने, चैत्र मास की नवमी तिथि को, अदिति देवता वाले नक्षत्र (पुनर्वसु) में और पाँच ग्रहों के उच्च राशि में स्थित होने पर... Thereafter, in the twelfth month, on the ninth day of the Chaitra month, when the star presided by Aditi (Punarvasu) was ascendant and five planets were in their exalted positions...
shloka.text: ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ । नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु पंचसु ॥ 2॥ तत्पश्चात् बारहवें महीने, चैत्र मास की नवमी तिथि को, अदिति देवता वाले नक्षत्र (पुनर्वसु) में और पाँच ग्रहों के उच्च राशि में स्थित होने पर... Thereafter, in the twelfth month, on the ninth day of the Chaitra month, when the star presided by Aditi (Punarvasu) was ascendant and five planets were in their exalted positions...
shloka.sanskrit: ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ । नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु पंचसु ॥ 2॥

shloka.english: Thereafter, in the twelfth month, on the ninth day of the Chaitra month, when the star presided by Aditi (Punarvasu) was ascendant and five planets were in their exalted positions...

shloka.raw_text: ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह । प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् । कौसल्याजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् ॥ 3॥ कर्कट लग्न में, चन्द्रमा के साथ बृहस्पति के उदित होते समय, कौसल्या ने सर्वलक्षणयुक्त, समस्त लोकों से वन्दित, जगत् के स्वामी श्रीराम को जन्म दिया। In the Cancer ascendant, with Jupiter conjoined with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to Rama, the Lord of the Universe, endowed with all auspicious marks and worshipped by all worlds.
shloka.text: ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह । प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् । कौसल्याजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् ॥ 3॥ कर्कट लग्न में, चन्द्रमा के साथ बृहस्पति के उदित होते समय, कौसल्या ने सर्वलक्षणयुक्त, समस्त लोकों से वन्दित, जगत् के स्वामी श्रीराम को जन्म दिया। In the Cancer ascendant, with Jupiter conjoined with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to Rama, the Lord of the Universe, endowed with all auspicious marks and worshipped by all worlds.

shloka.hindi: कर्कट लग्न में, चन्द्रमा के साथ बृहस्पति के उदित होते समय, कौसल्या ने सर्वलक्षणयुक्त, समस्त लोकों से वन्दित, जगत् के स्वामी श्रीराम को जन्म दिया।

shloka.raw_text: कौसल्यासुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते । उत्तिष्ट नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम् ॥ 4॥ हे कौसल्या के सुपुत्र राम! पूर्व दिशा में संध्या आरम्भ हो रही है। हे नरश्रेष्ठ! उठिए, दैवीय एवं दैनिक कर्म करने योग्य हैं। O Rama, noble son of Kausalya! The eastern dawn is breaking. Arise, O Tiger among men, the divine daily duties are to be performed.
shloka.text: कौसल्यासुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते । उत्तिष्ट नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम् ॥ 4॥ हे कौसल्या के सुपुत्र राम! पूर्व दिशा में संध्या आरम्भ हो रही है। हे नरश्रेष्ठ! उठिए, दैवीय एवं दैनिक कर्म करने योग्य हैं। O Rama, noble son of Kausalya! The eastern dawn is breaking. Arise, O Tiger among men, the divine daily duties are to be performed.
shloka.sanskrit: कौसल्यासुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते । उत्तिष्ट नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम् ॥ 4॥

shloka.english: O Rama, noble son of Kausalya! The eastern dawn is breaking. Arise, O Tiger among men, the divine daily duties are to be performed.

shloka.raw_text: ततः सीतां समानीय सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् । विद्युत्प्रभां विशालाक्षीं स्निग्धकुंचितमूर्धजाम् ॥ 5॥ तब सब आभूषणों से विभूषित, बिजली के समान कान्ति वाली, विशाल नेत्रों वाली, सुस्निग्ध घुँघराले केशों वाली सीता को लाकर... Then bringing Sita, adorned with all ornaments, resplendent as lightning, with large eyes and soft curling hair...
shloka.text: ततः सीतां समानीय सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् । विद्युत्प्रभां विशालाक्षीं स्निग्धकुंचितमूर्धजाम् ॥ 5॥ तब सब आभूषणों से विभूषित, बिजली के समान कान्ति वाली, विशाल नेत्रों वाली, सुस्निग्ध घुँघराले केशों वाली सीता को लाकर... Then bringing Sita, adorned with all ornaments, resplendent as lightning, with large eyes and soft curling hair...

shloka.raw_text: हंसांकितेन क्षौमेण किंचित्पीतेन संवृताम् । वासितेनोत्तरीयेण सुरक्तेण सुसंवृताम् ॥ 6॥ जो हंस के चिह्नों वाले कुछ पीले रंग के रेशमी वस्त्र से ढँकी थीं और सुगन्धित सुन्दर लाल रंग की चुनरी ओढ़े हुए थीं। Clad in a silken garment of slightly yellow hue marked with swans, and well-wrapped in a fragrant, beautiful red upper cloth.
shloka.text: हंसांकितेन क्षौमेण किंचित्पीतेन संवृताम् । वासितेनोत्तरीयेण सुरक्तेण सुसंवृताम् ॥ 6॥ जो हंस के चिह्नों वाले कुछ पीले रंग के रेशमी वस्त्र से ढँकी थीं और सुगन्धित सुन्दर लाल रंग की चुनरी ओढ़े हुए थीं। Clad in a silken garment of slightly yellow hue marked with swans, and well-wrapped in a fragrant, beautiful red upper cloth.
shloka.sanskrit: हंसांकितेन क्षौमेण किंचित्पीतेन संवृताम् । वासितेनोत्तरीयेण सुरक्तेण सुसंवृताम् ॥ 6॥
shloka.hindi: जो हंस के चिह्नों वाले कुछ पीले रंग के रेशमी वस्त्र से ढँकी थीं और सुगन्धित सुन्दर लाल रंग की चुनरी ओढ़े हुए थीं।
shloka.english: Clad in a silken garment of slightly yellow hue marked with swans, and well-wrapped in a fragrant, beautiful red upper cloth.

shloka.raw_text: समक्षमग्नेः संस्थाप्य राघवाभिमुखे तदा । अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम् ॥ 7॥ तब अग्नि के समक्ष राघव के सामने खड़ा करके राजा जनक ने कौसल्या के आनन्द को बढ़ाने वाले राम से कहा। Then placing her before the fire, facing Raghava, King Janaka spoke to the enhancer of Kausalya's joy.
shloka.text: समक्षमग्नेः संस्थाप्य राघवाभिमुखे तदा । अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम् ॥ 7॥ तब अग्नि के समक्ष राघव के सामने खड़ा करके राजा जनक ने कौसल्या के आनन्द को बढ़ाने वाले राम से कहा। Then placing her before the fire, facing Raghava, King Janaka spoke to the enhancer of Kausalya's joy.
shloka.sanskrit: समक्षमग्नेः संस्थाप्य राघवाभिमुखे तदा । अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम् ॥ 7॥
shloka.hindi: तब अग्नि के समक्ष राघव के सामने खड़ा करके राजा जनक ने कौसल्या के आनन्द को बढ़ाने वाले राम से कहा।
shloka.english: Then placing her before the fire, facing Raghava, King Janaka spoke to the enhancer of Kausalya's joy.

shloka.raw_text: इयं सीता मम सुता सहधर्मचरी तव । प्रतीच्छ चैनां भद्रं ते पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना।पतिव्रता महाभागा छायेवानुगता सदा॥ 8॥ यह सीता मेरी पुत्री है, तुम्हारी सहधर्मचारिणी होगी। इसका पाणिग्रहण करो। तुम्हारा कल्याण हो। यह पतिव्रता, महाभागा सदा छाया के समान तुम्हारा अनुसरण करेगी। This is Sita, my daughter, who will be your partner in Dharma. Accept her, may you be blessed, take her hand in yours. This greatly fortunate, devoted wife will ever follow you like a shadow.
shloka.text: इयं सीता मम सुता सहधर्मचरी तव । प्रतीच्छ चैनां भद्रं ते पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना।पतिव्रता महाभागा छायेवानुगता सदा॥ 8॥ यह सीता मेरी पुत्री है, तुम्हारी सहधर्मचारिणी होगी। इसका पाणिग्रहण करो। तुम्हारा कल्याण हो। यह पतिव्रता, महाभागा सदा छाया के समान तुम्हारा अनुसरण करेगी। This is Sita, my daughter, who will be your partner in Dharma. Accept her, may you be blessed, take her hand in yours. This greatly fortunate, devoted wife will ever follow you like a shadow.

shloka.hindi: यह सीता मेरी पुत्री है, तुम्हारी सहधर्मचारिणी होगी। इसका पाणिग्रहण करो। तुम्हारा कल्याण हो। यह पतिव्रता, महाभागा सदा छाया के समान तुम्हारा अनुसरण करेगी।
shloka.english: This is Sita, my daughter, who will be your partner in Dharma. Accept her, may you be blessed, take her hand in yours. This greatly fortunate, devoted wife will ever follow you like a shadow.

shloka.raw_text: गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं लोके विख्यातपौरुषम् । दीर्घबाहुं महासत्वं मत्तमातङ्ग‌गामिनम् ॥ 9॥ जो गन्धर्वराज के समान सुन्दर हैं, जिनका पौरुष विश्व में प्रसिद्ध है, जिनकी भुजाएँ लम्बी हैं, महान् सत्त्वशाली हैं और मतवाले हाथी के समान जिनकी चाल है। Resembling the King of Gandharvas, renowned in the world for valor, long-armed, of mighty prowess, and with the gait of an intoxicated elephant.
shloka.text: गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं लोके विख्यातपौरुषम् । दीर्घबाहुं महासत्वं मत्तमातङ्ग‌गामिनम् ॥ 9॥ जो गन्धर्वराज के समान सुन्दर हैं, जिनका पौरुष विश्व में प्रसिद्ध है, जिनकी भुजाएँ लम्बी हैं, महान् सत्त्वशाली हैं और मतवाले हाथी के समान जिनकी चाल है। Resembling the King of Gandharvas, renowned in the world for valor, long-armed, of mighty prowess, and with the gait of an intoxicated elephant.
shloka.sanskrit: गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं लोके विख्यातपौरुषम् । दीर्घबाहुं महासत्वं मत्तमातङ्ग‌गामिनम् ॥ 9॥
shloka.hindi: जो गन्धर्वराज के समान सुन्दर हैं, जिनका पौरुष विश्व में प्रसिद्ध है, जिनकी भुजाएँ लम्बी हैं, महान् सत्त्वशाली हैं और मतवाले हाथी के समान जिनकी चाल है।
shloka.english: Resembling the King of Gandharvas, renowned in the world for valor, long-armed, of mighty prowess, and with the gait of an intoxicated elephant.

shloka.raw_text: चन्द्रकान्ताननं रामं अतीवप्रियदर्शनम् । रूपौदार्यगुणैः पुंसां दृष्टिचित्तापहारिणम् ॥ 10॥ जिनका मुख चन्द्रमा के समान कान्तिमान् है, जो अत्यन्त प्रियदर्शन हैं तथा अपने रूप, उदारता और गुणों से मनुष्यों की दृष्टि और चित्त को चुरा लेते हैं। Whose face is lovely as the moon, exceedingly pleasing to behold, captivating the eyes and hearts of men with His beauty, generosity and virtues.
shloka.text: चन्द्रकान्ताननं रामं अतीवप्रियदर्शनम् । रूपौदार्यगुणैः पुंसां दृष्टिचित्तापहारिणम् ॥ 10॥ जिनका मुख चन्द्रमा के समान कान्तिमान् है, जो अत्यन्त प्रियदर्शन हैं तथा अपने रूप, उदारता और गुणों से मनुष्यों की दृष्टि और चित्त को चुरा लेते हैं। Whose face is lovely as the moon, exceedingly pleasing to behold, captivating the eyes and hearts of men with His beauty, generosity and virtues.

shloka.hindi: जिनका मुख चन्द्रमा के समान कान्तिमान् है, जो अत्यन्त प्रियदर्शन हैं तथा अपने रूप, उदारता और गुणों से मनुष्यों की दृष्टि और चित्त को चुरा लेते हैं।
shloka.english: Whose face is lovely as the moon, exceedingly pleasing to behold, captivating the eyes and hearts of men with His beauty, generosity and virtues.

shloka.raw_text: यं मुहूर्तमपश्यंस्तु न जीवेयमहं ध्रुवम् । तेन रामेण कैकेयि शपे ते वचनक्रियाम् ॥ 11॥ हे कैकेयी! जिन राम को एक क्षण भी न देखकर मैं निश्चय ही जीवित नहीं रह सकता, उन राम की शपथ लेकर मैं तुम्हारे वचन का पालन करूँगा। O Kaikeyi, I swear by Rama, without seeing whom even for a moment I surely cannot live, that I shall carry out your words.
shloka.text: यं मुहूर्तमपश्यंस्तु न जीवेयमहं ध्रुवम् । तेन रामेण कैकेयि शपे ते वचनक्रियाम् ॥ 11॥ हे कैकेयी! जिन राम को एक क्षण भी न देखकर मैं निश्चय ही जीवित नहीं रह सकता, उन राम की शपथ लेकर मैं तुम्हारे वचन का पालन करूँगा। O Kaikeyi, I swear by Rama, without seeing whom even for a moment I surely cannot live, that I shall carry out your words.
shloka.sanskrit: यं मुहूर्तमपश्यंस्तु न जीवेयमहं ध्रुवम् । तेन रामेण कैकेयि शपे ते वचनक्रियाम् ॥ 11॥
shloka.hindi: हे कैकेयी! जिन राम को एक क्षण भी न देखकर मैं निश्चय ही जीवित नहीं रह सकता, उन राम की शपथ लेकर मैं तुम्हारे वचन का पालन करूँगा।
shloka.english: O Kaikeyi, I swear by Rama, without seeing whom even for a moment I surely cannot live, that I shall carry out your words.

shloka.raw_text: सत्येन लोकान् जयति दीनान्दानेन राघवः। गुरून्शुश्रूषया वीरो धनुषा युधि शात्रवान् ॥ 12॥ राघव सत्य के द्वारा लोकों को जीतते हैं, दान से दीनों को, सेवा से गुरुजनों को तथा धनुष के द्वारा युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीतते हैं। Raghava conquers the worlds by truth, the poor by charity, the elders by service, and the enemies in battle by His bow.
shloka.text: सत्येन लोकान् जयति दीनान्दानेन राघवः। गुरून्शुश्रूषया वीरो धनुषा युधि शात्रवान् ॥ 12॥ राघव सत्य के द्वारा लोकों को जीतते हैं, दान से दीनों को, सेवा से गुरुजनों को तथा धनुष के द्वारा युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीतते हैं। Raghava conquers the worlds by truth, the poor by charity, the elders by service, and the enemies in battle by His bow.
shloka.sanskrit: सत्येन लोकान् जयति दीनान्दानेन राघवः। गुरून्शुश्रूषया वीरो धनुषा युधि शात्रवान् ॥ 12॥
shloka.hindi: राघव सत्य के द्वारा लोकों को जीतते हैं, दान से दीनों को, सेवा से गुरुजनों को तथा धनुष के द्वारा युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीतते हैं।
shloka.english: Raghava conquers the worlds by truth, the poor by charity, the elders by service, and the enemies in battle by His bow.

shloka.raw_text: तं वैश्रवणसङ्काशं उपविष्टं स्वलङ्कृतम् । ददर्श सूतः पर्यङ्के सौवर्णे सोत्तरच्छदे ॥ 13॥ सारथि ने देखा कि कुबेर के समान कान्ति वाले, सुसज्जित श्रीराम सोने के पलंग पर, जिसके ऊपर चँदवा तना है, विराजमान हैं। The charioteer saw Him, resplendent like Kubera, well-adorned, seated on a golden couch with a canopy overhead.
shloka.text: तं वैश्रवणसङ्काशं उपविष्टं स्वलङ्कृतम् । ददर्श सूतः पर्यङ्के सौवर्णे सोत्तरच्छदे ॥ 13॥ सारथि ने देखा कि कुबेर के समान कान्ति वाले, सुसज्जित श्रीराम सोने के पलंग पर, जिसके ऊपर चँदवा तना है, विराजमान हैं। The charioteer saw Him, resplendent like Kubera, well-adorned, seated on a golden couch with a canopy overhead.
shloka.sanskrit: तं वैश्रवणसङ्काशं उपविष्टं स्वलङ्कृतम् । ददर्श सूतः पर्यङ्के सौवर्णे सोत्तरच्छदे ॥ 13॥
shloka.hindi: सारथि ने देखा कि कुबेर के समान कान्ति वाले, सुसज्जित श्रीराम सोने के पलंग पर, जिसके ऊपर चँदवा तना है, विराजमान हैं।
shloka.english: The charioteer saw Him, resplendent like Kubera, well-adorned, seated on a golden couch with a canopy overhead.

shloka.raw_text: स्थितया पार्श्वतश्चापि वालव्यजनहस्तया । उपेतं सीतया भूयश्चित्रया शशिनं यथा ॥ 14॥ और पास ही हाथ में चँवर लिए खड़ी हुई सीता के साथ वे ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे थे जैसे चित्रा नक्षत्र के साथ चन्द्रमा। And attended by Sita standing nearby with a yak-tail fan in hand, He shone all the more like the moon with the star Chitra.
shloka.text: स्थितया पार्श्वतश्चापि वालव्यजनहस्तया । उपेतं सीतया भूयश्चित्रया शशिनं यथा ॥ 14॥ और पास ही हाथ में चँवर लिए खड़ी हुई सीता के साथ वे ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे थे जैसे चित्रा नक्षत्र के साथ चन्द्रमा। And attended by Sita standing nearby with a yak-tail fan in hand, He shone all the more like the moon with the star Chitra.
shloka.sanskrit: स्थितया पार्श्वतश्चापि वालव्यजनहस्तया । उपेतं सीतया भूयश्चित्रया शशिनं यथा ॥ 14॥
shloka.hindi: और पास ही हाथ में चँवर लिए खड़ी हुई सीता के साथ वे ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे थे जैसे चित्रा नक्षत्र के साथ चन्द्रमा।
shloka.english: And attended by Sita standing nearby with a yak-tail fan in hand, He shone all the more like the moon with the star Chitra.

shloka.raw_text: तं तपन्तमिवादित्यमुपपन्नं स्वतेजसा । ववन्दे वरदं वन्दी विनयज्ञो विनीतवत् ॥ 15॥ अपने तेज से सूर्य के समान तपते हुए, वर देने वाले उन राम को विनयज्ञ वन्दी ने विनीत भाव से प्रणाम किया। That bestower of boons, glowing like the sun with His own splendor, the bard, knowing humility, bowed to respectfully.
shloka.text: तं तपन्तमिवादित्यमुपपन्नं स्वतेजसा । ववन्दे वरदं वन्दी विनयज्ञो विनीतवत् ॥ 15॥ अपने तेज से सूर्य के समान तपते हुए, वर देने वाले उन राम को विनयज्ञ वन्दी ने विनीत भाव से प्रणाम किया। That bestower of boons, glowing like the sun with His own splendor, the bard, knowing humility, bowed to respectfully.
shloka.sanskrit: तं तपन्तमिवादित्यमुपपन्नं स्वतेजसा । ववन्दे वरदं वन्दी विनयज्ञो विनीतवत् ॥ 15॥
shloka.hindi: अपने तेज से सूर्य के समान तपते हुए, वर देने वाले उन राम को विनयज्ञ वन्दी ने विनीत भाव से प्रणाम किया।
shloka.english: That bestower of boons, glowing like the sun with His own splendor, the bard, knowing humility, bowed to respectfully.

shloka.raw_text: न हि तस्मान्मनः कश्चिच्चक्षुषी वा नरोत्तमात् । नरः शक्नोत्यपाक्रष्टुमतिक्रान्तेपि राघवे ॥ 16॥ राघव के चले जाने पर भी कोई मनुष्य उन नरोत्तम से अपना मन अथवा नेत्र नहीं हटा सकता था। Even after Raghava had departed, no man could withdraw his mind or eyes from that Best of Men.
shloka.text: न हि तस्मान्मनः कश्चिच्चक्षुषी वा नरोत्तमात् । नरः शक्नोत्यपाक्रष्टुमतिक्रान्तेपि राघवे ॥ 16॥ राघव के चले जाने पर भी कोई मनुष्य उन नरोत्तम से अपना मन अथवा नेत्र नहीं हटा सकता था। Even after Raghava had departed, no man could withdraw his mind or eyes from that Best of Men.
shloka.sanskrit: न हि तस्मान्मनः कश्चिच्चक्षुषी वा नरोत्तमात् । नरः शक्नोत्यपाक्रष्टुमतिक्रान्तेपि राघवे ॥ 16॥
shloka.hindi: राघव के चले जाने पर भी कोई मनुष्य उन नरोत्तम से अपना मन अथवा नेत्र नहीं हटा सकता था।
shloka.english: Even after Raghava had departed, no man could withdraw his mind or eyes from that Best of Men.

shloka.raw_text: यश्च रामं न पश्येत्तु यञ्च रामो न पश्यति । निन्दितः स वसेल्लोके स्वात्माप्येनं विगर्हते ॥ 17॥ जो राम को नहीं देखता और जिसे राम नहीं देखते, वह संसार में निन्दित होकर रहता है और उसका अपना आत्मा भी उसकी निन्दा करता है। He who does not see Rama, and whom Rama does not see, dwells condemned in the world, and even his own self despises him.
shloka.text: यश्च रामं न पश्येत्तु यञ्च रामो न पश्यति । निन्दितः स वसेल्लोके स्वात्माप्येनं विगर्हते ॥ 17॥ जो राम को नहीं देखता और जिसे राम नहीं देखते, वह संसार में निन्दित होकर रहता है और उसका अपना आत्मा भी उसकी निन्दा करता है। He who does not see Rama, and whom Rama does not see, dwells condemned in the world, and even his own self despises him.
shloka.sanskrit: यश्च रामं न पश्येत्तु यञ्च रामो न पश्यति । निन्दितः स वसेल्लोके स्वात्माप्येनं विगर्हते ॥ 17॥
shloka.hindi: जो राम को नहीं देखता और जिसे राम नहीं देखते, वह संसार में निन्दित होकर रहता है और उसका अपना आत्मा भी उसकी निन्दा करता है।
shloka.english: He who does not see Rama, and whom Rama does not see, dwells condemned in the world, and even his own self despises him.

shloka.raw_text: सर्वेषां हि स धर्मात्मा वर्णानां कुरुते दयाम् । चतुर्णां हि वयस्थानां तेन ते तमनुव्रताः ॥ 18॥ वे धर्मात्मा सभी वर्णों और चारों अवस्थाओं (आश्रमों) के लोगों पर दया करते हैं, इसीलिए वे सब उनके अनुगामी हैं। That righteous-souled one shows compassion to all castes and all four stages of life, therefore they all are devoted to Him.
shloka.text: सर्वेषां हि स धर्मात्मा वर्णानां कुरुते दयाम् । चतुर्णां हि वयस्थानां तेन ते तमनुव्रताः ॥ 18॥ वे धर्मात्मा सभी वर्णों और चारों अवस्थाओं (आश्रमों) के लोगों पर दया करते हैं, इसीलिए वे सब उनके अनुगामी हैं। That righteous-souled one shows compassion to all castes and all four stages of life, therefore they all are devoted to Him.
shloka.sanskrit: सर्वेषां हि स धर्मात्मा वर्णानां कुरुते दयाम् । चतुर्णां हि वयस्थानां तेन ते तमनुव्रताः ॥ 18॥
shloka.hindi: वे धर्मात्मा सभी वर्णों और चारों अवस्थाओं (आश्रमों) के लोगों पर दया करते हैं, इसीलिए वे सब उनके अनुगामी हैं।
shloka.english: That righteous-souled one shows compassion to all castes and all four stages of life, therefore they all are devoted to Him.

shloka.raw_text: न चास्य महतीं लक्ष्मीं राज्यनाशोपकर्षति । लोककान्तस्य कान्तत्वाच्छीतरश्मेरिव क्षपा ॥ 19॥ राज्य के नष्ट होने का दुःख भी इनकी महान् शोभा को कम नहीं कर पाता, जैसे चन्द्रमा की शोभा को क्षपा (रात्रि का अन्धकार) कम नहीं कर पाती। Even the loss of the kingdom does not diminish His great splendor, because He is beloved of the world, just as the night (darkness) does not diminish the cool-rayed moon's loveliness.
shloka.text: न चास्य महतीं लक्ष्मीं राज्यनाशोपकर्षति । लोककान्तस्य कान्तत्वाच्छीतरश्मेरिव क्षपा ॥ 19॥ राज्य के नष्ट होने का दुःख भी इनकी महान् शोभा को कम नहीं कर पाता, जैसे चन्द्रमा की शोभा को क्षपा (रात्रि का अन्धकार) कम नहीं कर पाती। Even the loss of the kingdom does not diminish His great splendor, because He is beloved of the world, just as the night (darkness) does not diminish the cool-rayed moon's loveliness.
shloka.sanskrit: न चास्य महतीं लक्ष्मीं राज्यनाशोपकर्षति । लोककान्तस्य कान्तत्वाच्छीतरश्मेरिव क्षपा ॥ 19॥
shloka.hindi: राज्य के नष्ट होने का दुःख भी इनकी महान् शोभा को कम नहीं कर पाता, जैसे चन्द्रमा की शोभा को क्षपा (रात्रि का अन्धकार) कम नहीं कर पाती।
shloka.english: Even the loss of the kingdom does not diminish His great splendor, because He is beloved of the world, just as the night (darkness) does not diminish the cool-rayed moon's loveliness.

shloka.raw_text: धारयन्मनसा दुःखमिन्द्रियाणि निगृह्य च। प्रविवेशात्मवान्वेश्म मातुरप्रियशंसिवान् ॥ 20॥ मन ही मन दुःख धारण करते हुए और इन्द्रियों को वश में रखकर, आत्मवान् राम माता के महल में प्रविष्ट हुए, जहाँ वे अप्रिय समाचार सुनाने वाले थे। Bearing the sorrow in His mind and restraining His senses, the self-possessed Rama entered His mother's palace, as the bearer of unpleasant tidings.
shloka.text: धारयन्मनसा दुःखमिन्द्रियाणि निगृह्य च। प्रविवेशात्मवान्वेश्म मातुरप्रियशंसिवान् ॥ 20॥ मन ही मन दुःख धारण करते हुए और इन्द्रियों को वश में रखकर, आत्मवान् राम माता के महल में प्रविष्ट हुए, जहाँ वे अप्रिय समाचार सुनाने वाले थे। Bearing the sorrow in His mind and restraining His senses, the self-possessed Rama entered His mother's palace, as the bearer of unpleasant tidings.
shloka.sanskrit: धारयन्मनसा दुःखमिन्द्रियाणि निगृह्य च। प्रविवेशात्मवान्वेश्म मातुरप्रियशंसिवान् ॥ 20॥
shloka.hindi: मन ही मन दुःख धारण करते हुए और इन्द्रियों को वश में रखकर, आत्मवान् राम माता के महल में प्रविष्ट हुए, जहाँ वे अप्रिय समाचार सुनाने वाले थे।
shloka.english: Bearing the sorrow in His mind and restraining His senses, the self-possessed Rama entered His mother's palace, as the bearer of unpleasant tidings.

shloka.raw_text: कथं हि धेनुः स्वं वत्सं गच्छन्तं नानुगच्छति । अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि पुत्र यत्र गमिष्यसि ॥ 21॥ गाय अपने बछड़े के जाने पर भला उसके पीछे क्यों न जाएगी? हे पुत्र! जहाँ तुम जाओगे, मैं भी तुम्हारे पीछे चलूँगी। How can a cow not follow her departing calf? O son, wherever you go, I shall follow you.
shloka.text: कथं हि धेनुः स्वं वत्सं गच्छन्तं नानुगच्छति । अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि पुत्र यत्र गमिष्यसि ॥ 21॥ गाय अपने बछड़े के जाने पर भला उसके पीछे क्यों न जाएगी? हे पुत्र! जहाँ तुम जाओगे, मैं भी तुम्हारे पीछे चलूँगी। How can a cow not follow her departing calf? O son, wherever you go, I shall follow you.
shloka.sanskrit: कथं हि धेनुः स्वं वत्सं गच्छन्तं नानुगच्छति । अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि पुत्र यत्र गमिष्यसि ॥ 21॥
shloka.hindi: गाय अपने बछड़े के जाने पर भला उसके पीछे क्यों न जाएगी? हे पुत्र! जहाँ तुम जाओगे, मैं भी तुम्हारे पीछे चलूँगी।
shloka.english: How can a cow not follow her departing calf? O son, wherever you go, I shall follow you.

shloka.raw_text: धर्मो हि परमो लोके धर्मे सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् । धर्मसंश्रितमेतच्च पितुर्वचनमुत्तमम् ॥ 22॥ संसार में धर्म ही सर्वोपरि है, सत्य धर्म में ही प्रतिष्ठित है, और पिता का यह श्रेष्ठ वचन भी धर्म पर ही आश्रित है। Dharma is indeed supreme in the world, truth is established in Dharma, and this noble command of our father is also based on Dharma.
shloka.text: धर्मो हि परमो लोके धर्मे सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् । धर्मसंश्रितमेतच्च पितुर्वचनमुत्तमम् ॥ 22॥ संसार में धर्म ही सर्वोपरि है, सत्य धर्म में ही प्रतिष्ठित है, और पिता का यह श्रेष्ठ वचन भी धर्म पर ही आश्रित है। Dharma is indeed supreme in the world, truth is established in Dharma, and this noble command of our father is also based on Dharma.
shloka.sanskrit: धर्मो हि परमो लोके धर्मे सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् । धर्मसंश्रितमेतच्च पितुर्वचनमुत्तमम् ॥ 22॥
shloka.hindi: संसार में धर्म ही सर्वोपरि है, सत्य धर्म में ही प्रतिष्ठित है, और पिता का यह श्रेष्ठ वचन भी धर्म पर ही आश्रित है।
shloka.english: Dharma is indeed supreme in the world, truth is established in Dharma, and this noble command of our father is also based on Dharma.

shloka.raw_text: यं पालयसि धर्मं त्वं धृत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्त्वामभिरक्षतु ॥ 23॥ हे रघुश्रेष्ठ! तुम जिस धर्म का धैर्य और नियमपूर्वक पालन कर रहे हो, वही धर्म तुम्हारी रक्षा करे। O Tiger among Raghus, may that very Dharma which you are upholding with patience and discipline, protect you.
shloka.text: यं पालयसि धर्मं त्वं धृत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्त्वामभिरक्षतु ॥ 23॥ हे रघुश्रेष्ठ! तुम जिस धर्म का धैर्य और नियमपूर्वक पालन कर रहे हो, वही धर्म तुम्हारी रक्षा करे। O Tiger among Raghus, may that very Dharma which you are upholding with patience and discipline, protect you.
shloka.sanskrit: यं पालयसि धर्मं त्वं धृत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्त्वामभिरक्षतु ॥ 23॥
shloka.hindi: हे रघुश्रेष्ठ! तुम जिस धर्म का धैर्य और नियमपूर्वक पालन कर रहे हो, वही धर्म तुम्हारी रक्षा करे।
shloka.english: O Tiger among Raghus, may that very Dharma which you are upholding with patience and discipline, protect you.

shloka.raw_text: शुद्धात्मन्प्रेमभावाद्धि भविष्यामि विकल्मषा । भर्तारमनुगच्छन्ती भर्ता हि मम दैवतम् ॥ 24॥ हे शुद्धात्मन्! प्रेमभाव से पति का अनुसरण करती हुई मैं निष्पाप हो जाऊँगी, क्योंकि पति ही मेरे देवता हैं। O Pure-souled one! Following my husband out of love, I shall be free from sin, for my husband is my deity.
shloka.text: शुद्धात्मन्प्रेमभावाद्धि भविष्यामि विकल्मषा । भर्तारमनुगच्छन्ती भर्ता हि मम दैवतम् ॥ 24॥ हे शुद्धात्मन्! प्रेमभाव से पति का अनुसरण करती हुई मैं निष्पाप हो जाऊँगी, क्योंकि पति ही मेरे देवता हैं। O Pure-souled one! Following my husband out of love, I shall be free from sin, for my husband is my deity.
shloka.sanskrit: शुद्धात्मन्प्रेमभावाद्धि भविष्यामि विकल्मषा । भर्तारमनुगच्छन्ती भर्ता हि मम दैवतम् ॥ 24॥
shloka.hindi: हे शुद्धात्मन्! प्रेमभाव से पति का अनुसरण करती हुई मैं निष्पाप हो जाऊँगी, क्योंकि पति ही मेरे देवता हैं।
shloka.english: O Pure-souled one! Following my husband out of love, I shall be free from sin, for my husband is my deity.

shloka.raw_text: भक्तां पतिव्रतां दीनां मां समां सुखदुःखयोः। नेतुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ समानसुखदुःखिनीम् ॥ 25॥ हे काकुत्स्थ! भक्ति करने वाली, पतिव्रता, दीन तथा सुख-दुःख में समान रहने वाली, तुम्हारे साथ सुख-दुःख भोगने वाली मुझे तुम्हें साथ ले चलना ही उचित है। O Kakutstha, it is proper for you to take me, who am devoted, chaste, helpless, equal in joy and sorrow, and a sharer of your joys and sorrows.
shloka.text: भक्तां पतिव्रतां दीनां मां समां सुखदुःखयोः। नेतुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ समानसुखदुःखिनीम् ॥ 25॥ हे काकुत्स्थ! भक्ति करने वाली, पतिव्रता, दीन तथा सुख-दुःख में समान रहने वाली, तुम्हारे साथ सुख-दुःख भोगने वाली मुझे तुम्हें साथ ले चलना ही उचित है। O Kakutstha, it is proper for you to take me, who am devoted, chaste, helpless, equal in joy and sorrow, and a sharer of your joys and sorrows.
shloka.sanskrit: भक्तां पतिव्रतां दीनां मां समां सुखदुःखयोः। नेतुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ समानसुखदुःखिनीम् ॥ 25॥
shloka.hindi: हे काकुत्स्थ! भक्ति करने वाली, पतिव्रता, दीन तथा सुख-दुःख में समान रहने वाली, तुम्हारे साथ सुख-दुःख भोगने वाली मुझे तुम्हें साथ ले चलना ही उचित है।
shloka.english: O Kakutstha, it is proper for you to take me, who am devoted, chaste, helpless, equal in joy and sorrow, and a sharer of your joys and sorrows.

shloka.raw_text: भृत्यवत्सल तिष्ठन्तं भर्तृपुत्रगते पथि । भक्तं भृत्यं स्थितं स्थित्यां त्वं न मां हातुमर्हसि ॥ 26॥ हे भृत्यवत्सल! स्वामिपुत्र के मार्ग पर स्थित, भक्त और सेवक, मर्यादा में स्थित मुझे तुम्हें छोड़ना उचित नहीं है। O you who are affectionate to servants! It is not right for you to abandon me, your devoted servant, standing firm on the path taken by my master's son, ever abiding in propriety.
shloka.text: भृत्यवत्सल तिष्ठन्तं भर्तृपुत्रगते पथि । भक्तं भृत्यं स्थितं स्थित्यां त्वं न मां हातुमर्हसि ॥ 26॥ हे भृत्यवत्सल! स्वामिपुत्र के मार्ग पर स्थित, भक्त और सेवक, मर्यादा में स्थित मुझे तुम्हें छोड़ना उचित नहीं है। O you who are affectionate to servants! It is not right for you to abandon me, your devoted servant, standing firm on the path taken by my master's son, ever abiding in propriety.
shloka.sanskrit: भृत्यवत्सल तिष्ठन्तं भर्तृपुत्रगते पथि । भक्तं भृत्यं स्थितं स्थित्यां त्वं न मां हातुमर्हसि ॥ 26॥
shloka.hindi: हे भृत्यवत्सल! स्वामिपुत्र के मार्ग पर स्थित, भक्त और सेवक, मर्यादा में स्थित मुझे तुम्हें छोड़ना उचित नहीं है।
shloka.english: O you who are affectionate to servants! It is not right for you to abandon me, your devoted servant, standing firm on the path taken by my master's son, ever abiding in propriety.

shloka.raw_text: तव शुश्रूषणं मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन् । अयोध्यां देवलोकं वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्यहम् ॥ 27॥ वन में रहकर मैं सिर झुकाकर तुम्हारी सेवा करूँगा। मैं अयोध्या को अथवा देवलोक को भी सब प्रकार से त्यागता हूँ। Dwelling in the forest, I shall serve you with bowed head. I renounce Ayodhya or even the heavenly world in every way.
shloka.text: तव शुश्रूषणं मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन् । अयोध्यां देवलोकं वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्यहम् ॥ 27॥ वन में रहकर मैं सिर झुकाकर तुम्हारी सेवा करूँगा। मैं अयोध्या को अथवा देवलोक को भी सब प्रकार से त्यागता हूँ। Dwelling in the forest, I shall serve you with bowed head. I renounce Ayodhya or even the heavenly world in every way.
shloka.sanskrit: तव शुश्रूषणं मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन् । अयोध्यां देवलोकं वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्यहम् ॥ 27॥
shloka.hindi: वन में रहकर मैं सिर झुकाकर तुम्हारी सेवा करूँगा। मैं अयोध्या को अथवा देवलोक को भी सब प्रकार से त्यागता हूँ।
shloka.english: Dwelling in the forest, I shall serve you with bowed head. I renounce Ayodhya or even the heavenly world in every way.

shloka.raw_text: आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय । जीविष्याम्यहमेतेन ययातिरिव साधुषु ॥ 28॥ हे सूत! राम के बैठने, सोने और भोजन करने के समाचार कहा करो। इसी के सहारे मैं उसी प्रकार जीवित रहूँगा जैसे साधुओं के सत्संग से ययाति जीवित रहे थे। O Charioteer, narrate to me the sitting, sleeping, and eating of Rama. By that I shall live, just as Yayati lived in the company of the righteous.
shloka.text: आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय । जीविष्याम्यहमेतेन ययातिरिव साधुषु ॥ 28॥ हे सूत! राम के बैठने, सोने और भोजन करने के समाचार कहा करो। इसी के सहारे मैं उसी प्रकार जीवित रहूँगा जैसे साधुओं के सत्संग से ययाति जीवित रहे थे। O Charioteer, narrate to me the sitting, sleeping, and eating of Rama. By that I shall live, just as Yayati lived in the company of the righteous.
shloka.sanskrit: आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय । जीविष्याम्यहमेतेन ययातिरिव साधुषु ॥ 28॥
shloka.hindi: हे सूत! राम के बैठने, सोने और भोजन करने के समाचार कहा करो। इसी के सहारे मैं उसी प्रकार जीवित रहूँगा जैसे साधुओं के सत्संग से ययाति जीवित रहे थे।
shloka.english: O Charioteer, narrate to me the sitting, sleeping, and eating of Rama. By that I shall live, just as Yayati lived in the company of the righteous.

shloka.raw_text: गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिह्मं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता । नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता ॥ 29॥ वन में रहकर हाथी, सिंह या व्याघ्र को देखकर भी राम की भुजाओं का आश्रय लेने वाली सीता भय नहीं करती। Even seeing an elephant, a lion, or a tiger in the forest, she who has taken refuge in Rama's arms feels no fear.
shloka.text: गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिह्मं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता । नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता ॥ 29॥ वन में रहकर हाथी, सिंह या व्याघ्र को देखकर भी राम की भुजाओं का आश्रय लेने वाली सीता भय नहीं करती। Even seeing an elephant, a lion, or a tiger in the forest, she who has taken refuge in Rama's arms feels no fear.
shloka.sanskrit: गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिह्मं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता । नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता ॥ 29॥
shloka.hindi: वन में रहकर हाथी, सिंह या व्याघ्र को देखकर भी राम की भुजाओं का आश्रय लेने वाली सीता भय नहीं करती।
shloka.english: Even seeing an elephant, a lion, or a tiger in the forest, she who has taken refuge in Rama's arms feels no fear.

shloka.raw_text: रामं वा लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्याक्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता ॥ 30॥ जानकी तो राम और लक्ष्मण के पीछे चलते हुए अयोध्या से एक कोस की दूरी पर ही यह समझती हैं कि मानो वे विहार के लिए निकली हैं। Following Rama and Lakshmana, Janaki, even at a distance of a Kos from Ayodhya, feels as if she has gone on a pleasure trip.
shloka.text: रामं वा लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्याक्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता ॥ 30॥ जानकी तो राम और लक्ष्मण के पीछे चलते हुए अयोध्या से एक कोस की दूरी पर ही यह समझती हैं कि मानो वे विहार के लिए निकली हैं। Following Rama and Lakshmana, Janaki, even at a distance of a Kos from Ayodhya, feels as if she has gone on a pleasure trip.
shloka.sanskrit: रामं वा लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्याक्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता ॥ 30॥
shloka.hindi: जानकी तो राम और लक्ष्मण के पीछे चलते हुए अयोध्या से एक कोस की दूरी पर ही यह समझती हैं कि मानो वे विहार के लिए निकली हैं।
shloka.english: Following Rama and Lakshmana, Janaki, even at a distance of a Kos from Ayodhya, feels as if she has gone on a pleasure trip.

shloka.raw_text: दीर्घकालोषितस्तस्मिन् गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन् स्वञ्च चित्तं विलोभयन् ॥ 31॥ उस पर्वत पर बहुत दिनों से रहने वाले, पर्वतीय वनों को प्रिय मानने वाले राम, वैदेही की प्रसन्नता की कामना करते हुए और अपने चित्त को भी रिझाते हुए बोले। Having dwelt long on that mountain, the lover of mountain forests, desiring to please Vaidehi and also charming His own mind, spoke.
shloka.text: दीर्घकालोषितस्तस्मिन् गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन् स्वञ्च चित्तं विलोभयन् ॥ 31॥ उस पर्वत पर बहुत दिनों से रहने वाले, पर्वतीय वनों को प्रिय मानने वाले राम, वैदेही की प्रसन्नता की कामना करते हुए और अपने चित्त को भी रिझाते हुए बोले। Having dwelt long on that mountain, the lover of mountain forests, desiring to please Vaidehi and also charming His own mind, spoke.
shloka.sanskrit: दीर्घकालोषितस्तस्मिन् गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन् स्वञ्च चित्तं विलोभयन् ॥ 31॥
shloka.hindi: उस पर्वत पर बहुत दिनों से रहने वाले, पर्वतीय वनों को प्रिय मानने वाले राम, वैदेही की प्रसन्नता की कामना करते हुए और अपने चित्त को भी रिझाते हुए बोले।
shloka.english: Having dwelt long on that mountain, the lover of mountain forests, desiring to please Vaidehi and also charming His own mind, spoke.

shloka.raw_text: न राज्याद्भ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः । मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम् ॥ 32॥ हे भद्रे! इस रमणीय पर्वत को देखकर न तो मुझे राज्य से वंचित होने का दुःख सताता है और न मित्रों के वियोग का। O gentle lady, beholding this delightful mountain, neither the loss of my kingdom nor separation from my friends troubles my mind.
shloka.text: न राज्याद्भ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः । मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम् ॥ 32॥ हे भद्रे! इस रमणीय पर्वत को देखकर न तो मुझे राज्य से वंचित होने का दुःख सताता है और न मित्रों के वियोग का। O gentle lady, beholding this delightful mountain, neither the loss of my kingdom nor separation from my friends troubles my mind.
shloka.sanskrit: न राज्याद्भ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः । मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम् ॥ 32॥
shloka.hindi: हे भद्रे! इस रमणीय पर्वत को देखकर न तो मुझे राज्य से वंचित होने का दुःख सताता है और न मित्रों के वियोग का।
shloka.english: O gentle lady, beholding this delightful mountain, neither the loss of my kingdom nor separation from my friends troubles my mind.

shloka.raw_text: वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह । पश्यन्ती विविधान्भावान्मनोवाक्कायसंयतान् ॥ 33॥ हे वैदेहि! मन, वाणी और शरीर से संयमित रहने वाले मेरे साथ इस चित्रकूट पर्वत पर विविध प्राकृतिक दृश्यों को देखती हुई क्या तुम आनन्दित हो रही हो? O Vaidehi, do you take delight with me on this Chitrakuta mountain, beholding these various beautiful scenes, while I remain restrained in mind, speech, and body?
shloka.text: वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह । पश्यन्ती विविधान्भावान्मनोवाक्कायसंयतान् ॥ 33॥ हे वैदेहि! मन, वाणी और शरीर से संयमित रहने वाले मेरे साथ इस चित्रकूट पर्वत पर विविध प्राकृतिक दृश्यों को देखती हुई क्या तुम आनन्दित हो रही हो? O Vaidehi, do you take delight with me on this Chitrakuta mountain, beholding these various beautiful scenes, while I remain restrained in mind, speech, and body?
shloka.sanskrit: वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह । पश्यन्ती विविधान्भावान्मनोवाक्कायसंयतान् ॥ 33॥
shloka.hindi: हे वैदेहि! मन, वाणी और शरीर से संयमित रहने वाले मेरे साथ इस चित्रकूट पर्वत पर विविध प्राकृतिक दृश्यों को देखती हुई क्या तुम आनन्दित हो रही हो?
shloka.english: O Vaidehi, do you take delight with me on this Chitrakuta mountain, beholding these various beautiful scenes, while I remain restrained in mind, speech, and body?

shloka.raw_text: सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् । कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि ॥ 34॥ हे सीते! हे भामिनी! कमल और पुष्करों को डुबोती हुई, एक सखी के समान मन्दाकिनी नदी में अवगाहन करो। O Sita, O beautiful lady, plunge into the Mandakini river like a companion, submerging the lotuses and lilies.
shloka.text: सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् । कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि ॥ 34॥ हे सीते! हे भामिनी! कमल और पुष्करों को डुबोती हुई, एक सखी के समान मन्दाकिनी नदी में अवगाहन करो। O Sita, O beautiful lady, plunge into the Mandakini river like a companion, submerging the lotuses and lilies.
shloka.sanskrit: सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् । कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि ॥ 34॥
shloka.hindi: हे सीते! हे भामिनी! कमल और पुष्करों को डुबोती हुई, एक सखी के समान मन्दाकिनी नदी में अवगाहन करो।
shloka.english: O Sita, O beautiful lady, plunge into the Mandakini river like a companion, submerging the lotuses and lilies.

shloka.raw_text: तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि । अभिषिंचस्व चाद्यैव राज्येन मघवानिव ॥ 35॥ आपके उस दासभूत मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए और इन्द्र के समान आज ही राज्य पर अभिषिक्त हो जाइए। Please show grace to me, your servant, and get yourself crowned as king today itself, like Maghavan (Indra).
shloka.text: तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि । अभिषिंचस्व चाद्यैव राज्येन मघवानिव ॥ 35॥ आपके उस दासभूत मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए और इन्द्र के समान आज ही राज्य पर अभिषिक्त हो जाइए। Please show grace to me, your servant, and get yourself crowned as king today itself, like Maghavan (Indra).
shloka.sanskrit: तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि । अभिषिंचस्व चाद्यैव राज्येन मघवानिव ॥ 35॥
shloka.hindi: आपके उस दासभूत मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए और इन्द्र के समान आज ही राज्य पर अभिषिक्त हो जाइए।
shloka.english: Please show grace to me, your servant, and get yourself crowned as king today itself, like Maghavan (Indra).

shloka.raw_text: नात्मनः कामकारोस्ति पुरुषोयमनीश्वरः । इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति ॥ 36॥ मनुष्य अपनी इच्छा से कार्य करने में स्वतन्त्र नहीं है, वह अनीश्वर (अस्वतन्त्र) है। कृतान्त (दैव/काल) उसे इधर-उधर खींचता रहता है। Man is not independent to act according to his own will; he is not the master. Fate drags him here and there.
shloka.text: नात्मनः कामकारोस्ति पुरुषोयमनीश्वरः । इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति ॥ 36॥ मनुष्य अपनी इच्छा से कार्य करने में स्वतन्त्र नहीं है, वह अनीश्वर (अस्वतन्त्र) है। कृतान्त (दैव/काल) उसे इधर-उधर खींचता रहता है। Man is not independent to act according to his own will; he is not the master. Fate drags him here and there.
shloka.sanskrit: नात्मनः कामकारोस्ति पुरुषोयमनीश्वरः । इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति ॥ 36॥
shloka.hindi: मनुष्य अपनी इच्छा से कार्य करने में स्वतन्त्र नहीं है, वह अनीश्वर (अस्वतन्त्र) है। कृतान्त (दैव/काल) उसे इधर-उधर खींचता रहता है।
shloka.english: Man is not independent to act according to his own will; he is not the master. Fate drags him here and there.

shloka.raw_text: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ॥ 37॥ सभी संचयों का अन्त विनाश है, उन्नति का अन्त पतन है, संयोग का अन्त वियोग है और जीवन का अन्त मरण है। All accumulations end in decay, all elevations end in falls, all unions end in separation, and life ends in death.
shloka.text: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ॥ 37॥ सभी संचयों का अन्त विनाश है, उन्नति का अन्त पतन है, संयोग का अन्त वियोग है और जीवन का अन्त मरण है। All accumulations end in decay, all elevations end in falls, all unions end in separation, and life ends in death.
shloka.sanskrit: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ॥ 37॥
shloka.hindi: सभी संचयों का अन्त विनाश है, उन्नति का अन्त पतन है, संयोग का अन्त वियोग है और जीवन का अन्त मरण है।
shloka.english: All accumulations end in decay, all elevations end in falls, all unions end in separation, and life ends in death.

shloka.raw_text: चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमाश्रमम् । प्राहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 38॥ हे धर्मज्ञ! धर्म के ज्ञाता विद्वान् चारों आश्रमों में गृहस्थाश्रम को श्रेष्ठ कहते हैं, उसे तुम कैसे त्याग सकते हो? O knower of Dharma, the learned declare the householder's stage as the best among the four Ashramas. How can you abandon it?
shloka.text: चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमाश्रमम् । प्राहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 38॥ हे धर्मज्ञ! धर्म के ज्ञाता विद्वान् चारों आश्रमों में गृहस्थाश्रम को श्रेष्ठ कहते हैं, उसे तुम कैसे त्याग सकते हो? O knower of Dharma, the learned declare the householder's stage as the best among the four Ashramas. How can you abandon it?
shloka.sanskrit: चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमाश्रमम् । प्राहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 38॥
shloka.hindi: हे धर्मज्ञ! धर्म के ज्ञाता विद्वान् चारों आश्रमों में गृहस्थाश्रम को श्रेष्ठ कहते हैं, उसे तुम कैसे त्याग सकते हो?
shloka.english: O knower of Dharma, the learned declare the householder's stage as the best among the four Ashramas. How can you abandon it?

shloka.raw_text: सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्माश्रिता सदा । सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम् ॥ 39॥ संसार में सत्य ही ईश्वर है, लक्ष्मी सदा सत्य का ही आश्रय लेती है। सब कुछ सत्यमूल है, सत्य से बढ़कर कोई पद नहीं है। Truth alone is God in this world, prosperity (Lakshmi) ever rests on truth. Truth is the root of everything; there is no state higher than truth.
shloka.text: सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्माश्रिता सदा । सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम् ॥ 39॥ संसार में सत्य ही ईश्वर है, लक्ष्मी सदा सत्य का ही आश्रय लेती है। सब कुछ सत्यमूल है, सत्य से बढ़कर कोई पद नहीं है। Truth alone is God in this world, prosperity (Lakshmi) ever rests on truth. Truth is the root of everything; there is no state higher than truth.
shloka.sanskrit: सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्माश्रिता सदा । सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम् ॥ 39॥
shloka.hindi: संसार में सत्य ही ईश्वर है, लक्ष्मी सदा सत्य का ही आश्रय लेती है। सब कुछ सत्यमूल है, सत्य से बढ़कर कोई पद नहीं है।
shloka.english: Truth alone is God in this world, prosperity (Lakshmi) ever rests on truth. Truth is the root of everything; there is no state higher than truth.

shloka.raw_text: लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद्वा हिमवान्वा हिमं त्यजेत् । अतीयात्सागरो वेळां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः ॥ 40॥ लक्ष्मी चन्द्रमा को छोड़ दे, हिमालय हिम को त्याग दे, सागर अपनी मर्यादा लाँघ जाए, परन्तु मैं पिता की प्रतिज्ञा का उल्लंघन नहीं करूँगा। Fortune may forsake the moon, the Himalayas may shed their snow, the ocean may transgress its shore, but I will not violate my father's promise.
shloka.text: लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद्वा हिमवान्वा हिमं त्यजेत् । अतीयात्सागरो वेळां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः ॥ 40॥ लक्ष्मी चन्द्रमा को छोड़ दे, हिमालय हिम को त्याग दे, सागर अपनी मर्यादा लाँघ जाए, परन्तु मैं पिता की प्रतिज्ञा का उल्लंघन नहीं करूँगा। Fortune may forsake the moon, the Himalayas may shed their snow, the ocean may transgress its shore, but I will not violate my father's promise.
shloka.sanskrit: लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद्वा हिमवान्वा हिमं त्यजेत् । अतीयात्सागरो वेळां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः ॥ 40॥
shloka.hindi: लक्ष्मी चन्द्रमा को छोड़ दे, हिमालय हिम को त्याग दे, सागर अपनी मर्यादा लाँघ जाए, परन्तु मैं पिता की प्रतिज्ञा का उल्लंघन नहीं करूँगा।
shloka.english: Fortune may forsake the moon, the Himalayas may shed their snow, the ocean may transgress its shore, but I will not violate my father's promise.

shloka.raw_text: भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तदा । पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत्तदा ॥ 41॥ तब भ्राता की आज्ञा का पालन करने वाले और प्रतिज्ञा में दृढ़ रहने वाले भरत ने पादुकाओं का राज्याभिषेक करके स्वयं नन्दिग्राम में निवास किया। Then Bharata, obedient to his brother's words and firm in his vow, consecrated the sandals on the throne and resided in Nandigrama.
shloka.text: भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तदा । पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत्तदा ॥ 41॥ तब भ्राता की आज्ञा का पालन करने वाले और प्रतिज्ञा में दृढ़ रहने वाले भरत ने पादुकाओं का राज्याभिषेक करके स्वयं नन्दिग्राम में निवास किया। Then Bharata, obedient to his brother's words and firm in his vow, consecrated the sandals on the throne and resided in Nandigrama.
shloka.sanskrit: भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तदा । पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत्तदा ॥ 41॥
shloka.hindi: तब भ्राता की आज्ञा का पालन करने वाले और प्रतिज्ञा में दृढ़ रहने वाले भरत ने पादुकाओं का राज्याभिषेक करके स्वयं नन्दिग्राम में निवास किया।
shloka.english: Then Bharata, obedient to his brother's words and firm in his vow, consecrated the sandals on the throne and resided in Nandigrama.

shloka.raw_text: स वालव्यजनं छत्रं धारयामास स स्वयम् । भरतः शासनं सर्वं पादुकाभ्यां न्यवेदयत् ॥ 42॥ भरत ने स्वयं चँवर डुलाया और छत्र धारण किया। वे समस्त राजकाज पादुकाओं को ही समर्पित करते थे। Bharata himself held the yak-tail fan and the umbrella. He submitted all governance to the sandals.
shloka.text: स वालव्यजनं छत्रं धारयामास स स्वयम् । भरतः शासनं सर्वं पादुकाभ्यां न्यवेदयत् ॥ 42॥ भरत ने स्वयं चँवर डुलाया और छत्र धारण किया। वे समस्त राजकाज पादुकाओं को ही समर्पित करते थे। Bharata himself held the yak-tail fan and the umbrella. He submitted all governance to the sandals.
shloka.sanskrit: स वालव्यजनं छत्रं धारयामास स स्वयम् । भरतः शासनं सर्वं पादुकाभ्यां न्यवेदयत् ॥ 42॥
shloka.hindi: भरत ने स्वयं चँवर डुलाया और छत्र धारण किया। वे समस्त राजकाज पादुकाओं को ही समर्पित करते थे।
shloka.english: Bharata himself held the yak-tail fan and the umbrella. He submitted all governance to the sandals.

shloka.raw_text: रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम् । ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः ॥ 43॥ वनवासी लोग राम के रूप, गठन, शोभा, सुकुमारता और सुन्दर वेष को देखकर आश्चर्यचकित हो गए। The forest dwellers saw Rama's beauty, build, grace, tenderness, and fine attire and were filled with wonder.
shloka.text: रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम् । ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः ॥ 43॥ वनवासी लोग राम के रूप, गठन, शोभा, सुकुमारता और सुन्दर वेष को देखकर आश्चर्यचकित हो गए। The forest dwellers saw Rama's beauty, build, grace, tenderness, and fine attire and were filled with wonder.
shloka.sanskrit: रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम् । ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः ॥ 43॥
shloka.hindi: वनवासी लोग राम के रूप, गठन, शोभा, सुकुमारता और सुन्दर वेष को देखकर आश्चर्यचकित हो गए।
shloka.english: The forest dwellers saw Rama's beauty, build, grace, tenderness, and fine attire and were filled with wonder.

shloka.raw_text: वृक्षाद्वृक्षं प्रधावन्सः गिरेश्चाद्रीन्नदान्नदीम् । बभूव विलपन्रामः शोकपङ्कार्णवाप्लुतः ॥ 44॥ वृक्ष-वृक्ष, पर्वत-पर्वत और नदी-नदी दौड़ते हुए राम शोकरूपी कीचड़ के समुद्र में डूबकर विलाप करने लगे। Running from tree to tree, hill to hill, river to river, Rama lamented, plunged into an ocean of sorrow like a mire.
shloka.text: वृक्षाद्वृक्षं प्रधावन्सः गिरेश्चाद्रीन्नदान्नदीम् । बभूव विलपन्रामः शोकपङ्कार्णवाप्लुतः ॥ 44॥ वृक्ष-वृक्ष, पर्वत-पर्वत और नदी-नदी दौड़ते हुए राम शोकरूपी कीचड़ के समुद्र में डूबकर विलाप करने लगे। Running from tree to tree, hill to hill, river to river, Rama lamented, plunged into an ocean of sorrow like a mire.
shloka.sanskrit: वृक्षाद्वृक्षं प्रधावन्सः गिरेश्चाद्रीन्नदान्नदीम् । बभूव विलपन्रामः शोकपङ्कार्णवाप्लुतः ॥ 44॥
shloka.hindi: वृक्ष-वृक्ष, पर्वत-पर्वत और नदी-नदी दौड़ते हुए राम शोकरूपी कीचड़ के समुद्र में डूबकर विलाप करने लगे।
shloka.english: Running from tree to tree, hill to hill, river to river, Rama lamented, plunged into an ocean of sorrow like a mire.
